doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Closing remarks
summary: Fillius expresses gratitude, Rowe says no one has been more interesting, and they sign off.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I’m going to give you the opportunity to have the last word here. Do you have any last words that you’d like to put on tape here?

No, it’s been a wonderful experience, a wonderful opportunity to be able to do this. And I’m everlastingly grateful to you and to the powers that be at this college to make it happen, because I don’t think it would have happened otherwise. And we did something that really needs to be done. And if we can hold it together it’s going to be very valuable someday. And I feel very good about it because it’s something that’s bothered me for a long time. Plus the fact that you’ve got my records so you can play them, they relate to most of those people. So I wish you well.
Well I wish you well too and I will say of all the people I’ve met in this project, no one has been more interesting than you.
I don’t know whether that’s a compliment or not. I’ll accept it as such.
Thank you very much. © Fillius Jazz Archive -25-
